work.prompt:
You are a worker in a build loop on the plotplot umbrella (jahala/plotplot). Make the check below pass, honestly. Nobody reviews your prose; only the verifier's verdict counts.

## The loop
docs/tend2/tend2.tend2.html is tend2's fit loop on the umbrella map: does tend2 belong to the garden. Its first check is the fit contract F1 to F6 of docs/building-the-garden.md §3, proven by one script, scripts/fit/tend2.sh, against tend2 at the revision the umbrella pins: contracts/fixtures/garden.lock, judge tend2, pinned by git url and rev (jahala/tend, a public repository), the revision that first carries tend2's garden.json and .brand/products/tend2/.

## Your check (c1)
- (code) fit contract F1 to F6 pass for tend2 at the pinned version: manifest, SARIF from lint, standalone install, declared context cost, metric command, brand layer and footer · evidence: scripts/fit/tend2.sh

## Read first
CLAUDE.md, docs/building-the-garden.md §1 to §3 (the F1 to F6 table and the notes under it), scripts/fit/lib.sh (fit_repo_root, fit_platform, fit_lock_lookup, fit_clone, fit_fetch, fit_verify_sha256, fit_extract, fit_clean_path, fit_run, fit_discard_scratch, fit_sha256), scripts/fit/weeder.sh (the model for shape, prose, exit codes and the unevaluable convention: read it whole), contracts/manifest.schema.json, contracts/test/lib/validate-sarif.mjs and contracts/vendor/sarif-schema-2.1.0.json, .brand/components.md (the garden footer reference: the eight bed names in the garden row), petals/scripts/check.sh (the vendored petals check a page must pass with zero errors, run with --brand pointing at this repository's .brand). The loop file is your full context and is READ-ONLY for you (check states belong to the verifier).

## How this fits
scripts/fit/tend2.sh is a bash script run from the repository root with no arguments (every claim, in order) or with one claim name; it composes scripts/fit/lib.sh. It prints one line per assertion (ok / not ok / unevaluable), exits 0 when every assertion passed, 1 on any failure, 3 when a claim could not be evaluated on this machine (say why on stderr). A claim that cannot be proven standalone is reported unevaluable, never passed. The loop's other checks name claims this script does not carry yet (stamp-version, tried-required, friction, npm, injection-cap, empty-run): for any claim name it does not know, print `unevaluable <claim>: this script proves f1 to f6; the claim '<claim>' has no evidence in it yet` and exit 3, the way weeder.sh does. Delete only with trash, never rm; scratch under a mktemp directory put away with fit_discard_scratch.

Every claim reads tend2 from the clone the runner makes, never from any tend2 on this machine: resolve the judge with fit_lock_lookup on contracts/fixtures/garden.lock (it returns `git: {url, rev}`), clone it once per run with fit_clone into scratch, and build it there with its own commands (`npm ci` then the manifest's smoke commands, or `npm run build`), with a PATH from fit_clean_path that holds the clone's bin directory and the system directories only. Read the manifest at the clone's root; take the check command, the metric command, the faces and the declared context cost from it, never from this prompt, so the script works for the next revision the lock pins.

The six claims, each its own function:
- F1 manifest: garden.json at the clone's root validates against contracts/manifest.schema.json with `npx --no-install ajv validate -s contracts/manifest.schema.json -d <file> --spec=draft2020 -c ajv-formats` (node_modules are installed by setup). Its name is tend2 and its version is the lock's.
- F2 SARIF: the manifest's check command, run from the clone on the clone's own docs/tend2 map (or on a small fixture map you write under scratch if the clone has none), emits a log that validates through contracts/test/lib/validate-sarif.mjs against the vendored schema; the tool component's name is tend2 and its version is the manifest's.
- F3 standalone install: with the clean PATH, in the clone, the manifest's smoke commands run and exit 0 (build, typecheck, its own test suite, and its `next` face on its map), and `tend2 --version` from the clone's bin reports the manifest's version. If a smoke command needs a tool the clean PATH cannot provide (node itself is a system tool for this purpose), say which and report unevaluable.
- F4 declared context cost: the manifest declares context.upfront_tokens; measure what a session pays at start from the faces the manifest names: every skill description line under the skill paths the manifest and the clone's plugin manifest declare, plus the MCP tools' names and descriptions if the clone exposes them without a live server (a list face, a generated schema file, or the source of the tool definitions), at four characters per token; the measured cost is at or under the declared cost. If the MCP tool descriptions cannot be read without running a server, measure the skills, say so, and report the MCP part unevaluable rather than passing on a partial count.
- F5 metric committed: the manifest's metric command runs in the clone and what it writes equals what is committed at the pinned rev byte for byte (find the file the command writes; the manifest or the clone's docs say where). If the command needs a checkout state the clone does not carry, run what can run and report the rest unevaluable with the reason.
- F6 brand layer and footer: the clone carries .brand/products/tend2/ with identity, colors and voice, and the mark files the umbrella's brand rules ask for; the clone's index.html passes `petals/scripts/check.sh <page> --brand .brand` (this repository's .brand) with zero errors; its footer's garden row lists every bed named in .brand/components.md's garden row, with tend2's pill current.

## Your environment
- You are at the repository root of an isolated git worktree of jahala/plotplot. Work here directly. Setup ran npm ci, cargo build --release and plotplot lock verify, so the planted hooks find their judges.
- Leave your changes in the working tree; do not create branches, commit, or push.
- Green is: `bash scripts/fit/tend2.sh` exits 0 with every claim ok, or exits 3 only for a claim that is honestly unevaluable on this machine with its reason on stderr; `npm test` and `cargo test --quiet` stay green (npm test reports some contracts tests red as recorded; those are owed by beds and are not yours). The conductor then runs weeder check --strict on your diff and the pinned tend2 verifier on check 1 of docs/tend2/tend2.tend2.html, whose evidence is this script.
- Probe and scratch files go in .loop-scratch/ only. If genuinely blocked, write BLOCKED.md at the repository root with what you tried, what stopped you and what a fix needs, instead of faking a green.
- Delete with trash, never rm. Never git reset. Never initialise a repository in place.

## Rules
- Solve the class of claim, not an example: the script must work for the next tend2 revision by reading the lock and the manifest, never by hard-coding a rev, a version, a path inside the clone that the manifest names, or a number.
- Never weaken a claim to make it pass; report unevaluable with the reason instead. A claim that is red because tend2 falls short is reported not ok with what was observed and what was expected; that is a true finding, and the loop records it.
- Production quality, the smallest honest change, prose in sentence case with no em dashes anywhere, including comments.
- Your FINAL message must end with one line of the form `Tried: YYYY-MM-DD <what you did, what you rejected and why, anything the next worker must know>`; the conductor transcribes it into the loop page.
